basis: REPLAY on 19 harvested BTC15m windows (2026-10-28..11-02), chronological 11 train / 8 holdout. Openings and completions simulated; conservative fill rule (wire must trade through a resting price), queue ignored which is OPTIMISTIC on fills. Fees at venue-verified taker 0.0695 / maker rebate 0.0125, bankers cent. Incentives counted at ZERO. No look-ahead.

penalty_calibration.method: adverse-selection penalty per unit = (paid - redeemed)/unit on venue-settled residual legs, calibrated ONLY on legs settled BEFORE the tape begins (2026-10-28), so it is temporally out-of-sample w.r.t. the replay
penalty_calibration.reading: the ONLY band with positive risk-adjusted EV is own price BELOW 0.20, which the deployed band floor explicitly excludes. Every band the engine actually trades (proved to be 0.20-0.47 at depth 2) is negative.

arms.verdict: IDENTICAL to baseline. 44 BUDGET refusals changed no outcome: component 1 has NO measurable effect.
unstable: at lam=0 both sides have identical EV so the sort is an arbitrary tie-break. Noise, not signal.
REFUSES EVERY TRADE. 294 EV_NEGATIVE refusals, zero orders.
REFUSES EVERY TRADE -- the no-trade baseline in a policy costume
the only arm that both trades and improves holdout; but worsens train, and its edge rests on the sub-0.20 band (5 calibration legs / 8.86 units)
opening the floor WITHOUT the penalty is worse than baseline: the penalty is doing real filtering work in G7

refusal_disclosure: EXPLICIT, as asked: at the fully calibrated penalty (lam>=0.5) the policy refuses 100% of trades and returns exactly 0.0000. Its apparent improvement over a losing baseline is REFUSAL, not edge. No arm improves BOTH chronological halves.

l5_fidelity.cap_used: L5 own p95 |post_imb| = 427 contracts, so the budget is scaled to HIM not to our 2
l5_fidelity.verdict: Grok policy permits 5.7% of L5 actions and 0.5% of his openings. It does NOT explain L5; it is close to his complement. He puts 26.7% of actions above own 0.65 where our calibrated penalty says EV is -0.69.
l5_fidelity.why: our adverse-selection penalty is a property of OUR execution -- 2 contracts resting 2 ticks behind a 52,000-100,000 share touch -- not of the market. Applying it to a size-scale liquidity provider is a category error, which is what the 5.7% measures.

existing_controls_gap.quantity_only_gate: ValidationGates.refuse() gate 1 is abs(unmatched_after) > 5 contracts. 18 parameters, NO clock parameter and NO expected-value parameter (verified by signature inspection). 5 contracts at own 0.47 is .35 of adversely-selected residual; 5 at own 0.20 is .00; the gate treats them identically.
existing_controls_gap.static_price_band: the first-leg band [0.20,0.60] is a price filter derived ONCE from an out-of-sample EV curve on L5 history, never re-evaluated per order and blind to current inventory, so the 5th contract of residual passes the same test as the 1st
existing_controls_gap.dead_ev_machinery: l5_two_sided_probe.expected_value() has ZERO call sites; min_completion_probability() has 2, both outside the decision path. The machinery to do exactly what Grok proposes is already written and wired to nothing.
existing_controls_gap.only_economic_bound: max_worst_case_deficit_usd = 1.50 -- static, and a worst-case CASH bound rather than an expected-value test
existing_controls_gap.conclusion: the gap Grok names is REAL and is not a duplicate of an existing safeguard. Component 3 (completion) already works and was preserved untouched.
